title: Multimodal AI Fundamentals & Fusion
interviewAnswer: Multimodal models combine information from different modalities such as text, images, audio or video. The core problems are representation, alignment and fusion: encode each modality, place or project representations into a compatible space, and let the model combine them for prediction or generation.
why: Modern AI systems increasingly accept image, text and audio together; architecture questions often reduce to where and how modalities interact.
intuition: Different sensors speak different languages. The model needs translators for each modality and a meeting room where their representations can interact.
deepDive: Fusion can happen early at token/feature level, through cross-attention/joint attention, or late by combining independent predictions. Training objectives may be contrastive, generative or matching/alignment based. Challenges include unequal information content, missing modalities, temporal/spatial alignment and one modality dominating the prediction.
workedExample: For document question answering, a vision encoder represents page regions and a language model represents the question; cross-modal attention lets question tokens retrieve relevant visual/text regions.
commonMistakes: Assuming concatenating embeddings is always sufficient fusion.
Ignoring missing/noisy modalities and modality dominance.
followUps: How do you handle missing modalities?
production: Monitor each modality independently, validate preprocessing contracts and design fallbacks when one modality is missing or corrupted.
